thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — GeoDNS inconsistency alert: several probes show divergent A records for api.redwood.ai between Cloudflare resolvers and AWS Route53 NSs. Spike in client errors originating from eu-west-1 starting ~23:01 UTC. Threshold triggered: >12% NX/502 in 60s.

sarah (oncall): I'm online. Starting triage — raj, collect dig traces and check our probes. mike, any infra changes?

raj (sre): quick probes below:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai A
35.190.12.34
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai A
13.225.45.67
$ dig +short @ns-abc.awsdns-12.net api.redwood.ai A
13.225.45.67
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai TXT
"cf-proxied"
```
CF resolvers returning old/proxied IP (35.190.12.34) intermittently; Route53 NSs returning current origin (13.225.45.67). TTL previously 300s. Looks like stale cache or proxy delegation on CF side.

mike (netops): No Route53 changes from our side in 24h. Cloudflare health metrics show higher 502/504 counts at eu POPs and some POPs reporting origin unreachability. Could be Cloudflare edge health check flapping or partial POP outage.

olga (support): EU customers reporting sign-up failures and API 502s; prioritised list shared privately. Most incidents from customers pinned to eu-west-1.

james (pm): High-level ask — is this DNS-only or also origin-level failures?

raj (sre): curl tests:
```
$ curl -sS -I http://13.225.45.67/health
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
$ curl -sS -I http://35.190.12.34/health
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
So origin IP healthy but proxied IP returning 502. If CF resolvers hand out proxied IP, clients hit failing edge and see 502/504.

sarah (oncall): Mitigation plan (parallel): 1) lower Route53 TTL to 60s, 2) set a Route53 weighted/region override steering eu queries to healthy pool, 3) ask Mike to request CF flush or disable proxy for affected record as fallback. Raj — prepare commands. Mike — open CF support case.

raj (sre): CLI snippets:
```
# lower TTL
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"13.225.45.67"}]}}]}'

# weighted record for eu override
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"CREATE","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-failover","Weight":0,"Region":"eu-west-1","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"13.225.45.67"}]}}]}'
```
Note: may need to UPSERT instead of CREATE depending on existing sets. Rollback: TTL=300, delete weighted override.

mike (netops): Opened CF ticket #CF-98233, pasted dig output. Requested urgent cache purge and asked about proxied IP flush. Also prepped API call to disable proxy on that DNS record if purge fails: 
```
# disable CF proxy via API
curl -X PATCH "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/$ZONE_ID/dns_records/$RECORD_ID" \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: ops@redwood.ai" -H "X-Auth-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"type":"A","name":"api.redwood.ai","content":"13.225.45.67","proxied":false}'
```
This will bypass CF edge but removes caching and DDoS protection, so go/no-go depends on CF purge ETA.

olga (support): Recommend status update: "Investigating: EU customers in eu-west-1 experiencing intermittent errors. Engineers working on DNS failover and coordinating with Cloudflare. We'll update within 30m or on resolution."

sarah (oncall): James — can you post that on status.redwood.ai and ping our EU account owners?

james (pm): Posted short incident note: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-15-eu-resolver-issue. Pinging account owners now.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T23:04:12Z — route53-ttl-reduction — status: success (change id: R-22345)

raj (sre): TTL lowered to 60s and weighted override applied (change id R-22346). Awaiting CF purge. If CF keeps returning 35.190.12.34, we'll flip proxied=false.

mike (netops): CF acknowledged the purge request; estimated completion 8-10 minutes. I'll hold the disable-proxy action until we see no improvement.

olga (support): After TTL change, customer reports reduced errors. A few users still hit cached answers. Sending follow-up note to affected accounts.

sarah (oncall): Handing watch to Raj in ~20m. Raj — you take ownership at 23:20 UTC. If errors bump, escalate to SRE-1.

raj (sre): Taking over. Action items: 1) confirm CF purge across EU POPs, 2) if not cleared in 12m, disable CF proxy for the hostname, 3) monitor error rate and client success, 4) prepare post-incident timeline and draft RCA.

mike (netops): CF support reports most edges now serve correct IP 13.225.45.67; 2/12 edges still lagging and should clear within a few minutes. Continuing to monitor.

james (pm): Please capture peak error rate numbers — need to quantify impacted percent/users for customer comms.

raj (sre): quick metric: EU error rate peaked ~18% for the 10m window around 23:02 UTC; currently ~4% and trending down. Will calculate exact request counts for postmortem.

olga (support): Sent customer follow-up: "We've implemented DNS failover and worked with Cloudflare to purge stale caches. Some clients may still experience issues until resolver caches expire; recommend retrying requests. We'll provide a full timeline."

sarah (oncall): Handoff to raj completed at 23:20 UTC. Active changes: R-22345 (TTL change), R-22346 (eu-weight). If regression occurs, page SRE-1.

raj (sre): acknowledged — monitoring and will update final post-incident numbers.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and state set to 'monitoring' by raj (sre).
